flags.headline: EIX's unexplained -6.76% decline now identified: Eaton Fire liability still unquantifiable + credit-downgrade warning -- escalated from AMBER
flags.detail: EIX fell 6.76% on 7/31 (prev close $78.73 -> $73.41) despite beating Q2 core EPS ($1.54 vs $0.97 y/y) and reaffirming 2026 core EPS guidance of $5.90-$6.20. Q2 earnings-call/8-K disclosure: SCE has extended $775M+ in Eaton Fire compensation offers and crossed the $1B threshold for CA Wildfire Fund reimbursement, but management still cannot estimate even the low end of the GAAP loss range. Management also warned that a lack of credit-supportive legislation could push the utility into non-investment-grade territory. Barclays separately downgraded EIX (Overweight -> Equal-Weight, PT $78 -> $75). Friday's 8/1 report could not find a tier-1 catalyst for this move; today's research confirms one via the company's own Q2 disclosure.
flags.thesis_link: Matches EIX key_risk: 'Elevated debt-to-equity of 216% amplifies financial risk from future wildfire events... a single catastrophic fire in SCE's territory could create material liability.' The unquantifiable Eaton Fire GAAP liability and credit-downgrade warning are a direct materialization of this risk.
